shortDescription: A sponge soaked in three milks until custardy, one of the most-ordered desserts across Latin America.
The 'impossible cake' — chocolate cake and caramel flan that swap layers in the oven as they bake.
The centerpiece of Dominican birthdays, soaked in syrup and finished with glossy meringue buttercream.
Sweden's 'sticky cake', a thin fudgy chocolate bake meant to stay gooey at the center.
Wafer-thin honey layers rested for a day under sour-cream frosting until they soften into a torte.
A Breton laminated pastry cake, folded with layer upon layer of butter and sugar until it caramelizes.
Born at a small San Sebastián bar, this scorched crustless cheesecake later defined the 2020s worldwide.
A dense chocolate torte with a thin apricot jam layer, at the center of a decades-long ownership dispute between two Viennese institutions.
A Parsi bakery classic enriched with reduced milk solids and cardamom, found in Mumbai's Irani cafés.
A featherlight chiffon cake colored and flavored with pandan leaf, a staple across Southeast Asian bakeries.
A semolina cake soaked in orange blossom syrup, served across the Levant and North Africa.
A meringue-lightened cheesecake baked in a water bath until it jiggles like a cloud.
A tall honey sponge cake of Portuguese origin, brought by traders and adapted into a Nagasaki specialty.
Legend says a St. Louis baker mixed up the butter cake ratio by accident in the 1930s — the mistake stuck around.
Named for WWII-era blackout drills near the Brooklyn Navy Yard, this triple-chocolate cake was an Ebinger's Bakery icon.
Believed to have Jamaican roots before becoming the defining cake of Southern potlucks and church suppers.
Created by Emma Rylander Lane in the 1890s and later immortalized in Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird.
A staple of South African Sunday lunches, served warm with custard or ice cream to melt into the sauce.
The centerpiece of Christmas dinner in Australia and New Zealand, topped with whatever fruit is in season.
Named after a 19th-century Governor of Queensland, now celebrated every July 21 on National Lamington Day.
